module_title: Infrastructure Projects, Declaratory Decrees & Instrument Rectification
introduction: Tailored for advanced legal exams and UPSC Law Optional, this level explores the absolute ban on injunctions against national infrastructure projects, the nuances of Declaratory Decrees, and the equitable remedies of Rectification and Cancellation of Instruments.

core_concepts.title: Infrastructure Projects Shield (Section 20A)
core_concepts.description:
Added in 2018 to prevent frivolous litigation from stalling national progress.
- Rule: No court shall grant an injunction in a suit involving an Infrastructure Project (specified in the Schedule, e.g., highways, power plants, water sanitation) if granting the injunction would cause **delay or hindrance** in the progress or completion of that project.
- Special Courts: Section 20B mandates State Governments (with the Chief Justice of the HC) to designate Special Courts to exclusively try SRA suits relating to infrastructure projects.

core_concepts.title: Declaratory Decrees (Section 34)
core_concepts.description:
Used to remove 'clouds' over legal rights or titles.
- Concept: If a person's legal character or right to property is denied by someone else, they can file a suit asking the court to officially 'declare' their right. 
- The Proviso Trap: A court will NOT grant a mere declaration if the plaintiff is able to seek 'further relief' (like recovery of possession) but omits to do so. You cannot just ask for a declaration of ownership if you are also out of possession; you must ask for declaration *plus* possession.

core_concepts.title: Rectification of Instruments (Section 26)
core_concepts.description: If a written contract does not express the real intention of the parties due to **Fraud** or **Mutual Mistake**, either party can apply to the court to have the instrument 'rectified' (corrected). The court will fix the document to reflect what was originally agreed upon, without canceling the entire contract.

core_concepts.title: Rescission and Cancellation (Sections 27 & 31)
core_concepts.description:
- Rescission (Sec 27): Canceling a contract. Allowed if the contract is voidable or terminable by the plaintiff.
- Cancellation of Instruments (Sec 31): If a written instrument is void or voidable, and the plaintiff has a reasonable apprehension that if left outstanding it may cause them 'serious injury', they can sue to have it adjudged void and officially cancelled by the court.

important_entities.name: Time Limit for SRA Suits (Section 20C)
important_entities.key_fact: A strict disposal timeline added by the 2018 Amendment.
important_entities.significance: A suit filed under the SRA must be disposed of by the court within **12 months** from the date of service of summons to the defendant. This can be extended by a maximum of 6 months (total 18 months) for reasons recorded in writing.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In Cancellation of Instruments (Sec 31), if the instrument has been registered under the Indian Registration Act, the court must also send a copy of its decree to the registration officer, who will formally note the cancellation on their official books.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Fix it (26), Kill the Contract (27), Kill the Paper (31)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Section 26 is Rectification (Fixing). Section 27 is Rescission (Killing the legal contract). Section 31 is Cancellation (Killing the physical/legal document).

exam_strategy_tips: If an advanced Judiciary question asks 'Can a civil court issue a stay order halting the construction of a scheduled National Highway due to a land dispute?', the answer is **NO**, citing the strict prohibition under **Section 20A** regarding Infrastructure Projects.
